label: Drone landscapes
blurb: Landscapes that read from the air — always with the field brief first.

places.name: Múlafossur Waterfall
places.why: A waterfall drops straight off a sea cliff behind a village of a few houses; the classic Faroese drone shot.

places.name: Trælanípa & Sørvágsvatn
places.why: An optical illusion makes this lake look suspended far above the ocean on a sheer cliff edge.

places.name: Mykines bird cliffs
places.why: Puffin-covered cliffs on the westernmost Faroese island; a bird colony with seasonal nesting closures.

places.name: Nazaré (Praia do Norte)
places.why: An underwater canyon funnels the Atlantic into the biggest rideable waves on record beneath the lighthouse cliff.

places.name: Ponta da Piedade
places.why: Ochre sandstone arches, sea stacks and grottoes off Lagos read as a maze of shapes from directly above.

places.name: Étretat cliffs
places.why: Chalk cliffs with a natural arch and a needle of rock, painted by Monet and now a drone-photo staple.

places.name: Calanque d'En-Vau
places.why: A narrow turquoise fjord cut into white limestone; it sits inside a national park where France restricts drones.

places.name: Valensole lavender fields
places.why: Purple rows run to the horizon in July; the geometry only really shows from height.

places.name: Cliffs of Moher
places.why: Eight kilometres of Atlantic cliffs rising 200m; drone launches near the visitor centre are locally restricted.

places.name: Giant's Causeway
places.why: Forty thousand interlocking basalt columns meet the sea in a pattern that reads as pure geometry from above.

places.name: Seven Sisters cliffs
places.why: A rolling line of chalk cliffs and dry valleys along the English Channel, best lit in low morning sun.

places.name: Durdle Door
places.why: A limestone arch stands alone in the surf on England's Jurassic Coast.

places.name: Old Man of Storr & Quiraing
places.why: Landslipped pinnacles and terraces along a ridge above the sea, one of Skye's most-photographed skylines.

places.name: Fairy Pools
places.why: A chain of clear cascades and plunge pools below the Black Cuillin, small but graphic from directly overhead.

places.name: Glencoe
places.why: A glaciated valley of steep glens and ridgelines; a favourite for low, valley-length drone passes.

places.name: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock)
places.why: A flat granite platform juts 600m straight over Lysefjord with no railing at the edge.

places.name: Kjeragbolten
places.why: A boulder wedged in a crevasse a kilometre above the same fjord as Pulpit Rock, with climbers for scale.

places.name: Trolltunga
places.why: A tongue of rock juts horizontally over a lake 700m below; queues for the photo can be long in summer.

places.name: Geirangerfjord (Ørnesvingen)
places.why: Switchback road views over a narrow UNESCO fjord lined with waterfalls and abandoned farms.

places.name: Reine, Lofoten
places.why: Red fishing cabins on stilts sit between jagged peaks and the Norwegian Sea; midnight sun in summer.

places.name: Segla, Senja
places.why: A knife-edge peak drops straight into a fjord on Norway's second-largest island.

places.name: Svalbard glacier front
places.why: Calving glacier fronts meet the Arctic Ocean at 78°N; polar bear country, so travel is guided.

places.name: Skógafoss
places.why: A 60m curtain waterfall on the former sea cliff line, wide enough to fill a wide-angle frame from above.

places.name: Seljalandsfoss
places.why: A waterfall you can walk behind, on a cliff that was once Iceland's coastline.

places.name: Gullfoss
places.why: The Hvítá river drops in two stages into a canyon; spray and rainbows are near-constant in summer.

places.name: Dyrhólaey
places.why: A basalt arch and headland with black-sand beaches on both sides; part is a bird reserve closed in nesting season.

places.name: Reynisfjara
places.why: Black volcanic sand with hexagonal basalt columns and sea stacks just offshore.

places.name: Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon
places.why: Icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull drift out to sea past seals hauled out on the ice.

places.name: Diamond Beach
places.why: Clear ice chunks from the lagoon wash up and melt on black sand right at the surf line.

places.name: Fjaðrárgljúfur Canyon
places.why: A serpentine, moss-lined canyon; fragile ground has forced seasonal closures and it sits in a protected reserve.

places.name: Vestrahorn (Stokksnes)
places.why: A jagged basalt massif rises straight from black-sand tidal flats and dune grass.

places.name: Kirkjufell
places.why: A cone-shaped mountain by the sea with a small waterfall in front, often shot with the aurora overhead.

places.name: Landmannalaugar
places.why: Rhyolite mountains banded in red, green and gold; the reserve restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Skaftafell, Vatnajökull NP
places.why: Glacier tongues spill off Europe's largest ice cap; Vatnajökull National Park commonly restricts drone flights.

places.name: Svínafellsjökull
places.why: A crevassed glacier tongue used in Interstellar and Game of Thrones; inside a national park with drone limits.

places.name: Þórsmörk valley
places.why: A green valley wedged between three glaciers and reached mostly by river-fording 4x4; a protected nature reserve.

places.name: Aletsch Glacier
places.why: The longest glacier in the Alps, a slow river of ice inside a UNESCO World Heritage area.

places.name: Gornergrat (Matterhorn)
places.why: A ridge-top railway station faces the Matterhorn's pyramid across a glacier valley.

places.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
places.why: Three sheer limestone towers rise from an alpine plateau inside a protected nature park.

places.name: Seceda ridge
places.why: A jagged Dolomite ridgeline drops into green pasture, one of the most-shared alpine drone shots.

places.name: Positano, Amalfi Coast
places.why: Pastel houses stack up a cliff straight from the Tyrrhenian Sea.

places.name: Manarola, Cinque Terre
places.why: A fishing village clings to a cliff above the sea; the national park restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Mount Etna craters
places.why: Europe's most active volcano; the park restricts drones near the summit craters, more so during eruptions.

places.name: Stromboli
places.why: A permanently erupting volcanic island, throwing incandescent bombs after dark most nights.

places.name: Santorini caldera (Oia)
places.why: White cube houses ring the rim of a collapsed volcanic caldera above the Aegean.

places.name: Navagio (Shipwreck) Beach
places.why: A rusted shipwreck sits on a white-sand cove reachable only by boat, ringed by sheer limestone cliffs.

places.name: Meteora
places.why: Monasteries balance atop sandstone pillars that rise straight out of the plain.

places.name: Samaria Gorge
places.why: One of Europe's longest gorges, inside a national park where drone flights are commonly restricted.

places.name: Vikos Gorge
places.why: One of the world's deepest gorges relative to width, seen from the Oxya viewpoint above Monodendri.

places.name: Plitvice Lakes
places.why: Sixteen terraced turquoise lakes connected by waterfalls; the national park bans drones without special permission.

places.name: Krka Waterfalls
places.why: Travertine cascades step down through forest into the Krka river; the national park restricts drones.

places.name: Tara River Canyon
places.why: Europe's deepest canyon, cut by a river popular with rafters, spanned by a single high bridge.

places.name: Pamukkale
places.why: Blinding-white travertine terraces of mineral pools cascade down a hillside like frozen rice paddies.

places.name: Cappadocia (Göreme valleys)
places.why: Wind-carved fairy chimneys and valleys fill with hundreds of balloons at sunrise; drone flights need a permit here.

places.name: Keukenhof tulip fields
places.why: Ruler-straight rows of tulips in primary colours, best read as pure pattern from directly overhead.

places.name: Teide National Park
places.why: Spain's highest peak sits in a volcanic caldera above a sea of clouds; the park restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Caminito del Rey gorge
places.why: A walkway pinned to a limestone gorge wall above the Guadalhorce River.

places.name: Sete Cidades
places.why: Twin crater lakes, one blue and one green, fill an extinct volcano's caldera.

places.name: Ponta de São Lourenço
places.why: A narrow, wind-scoured peninsula of red and green volcanic rock reaching into the Atlantic.

places.name: Sossusvlei & Deadvlei
places.why: Deep-red dunes surround a dead clay pan of ancient blackened trees; the national park requires a drone permit.

places.name: Sesriem Canyon
places.why: A narrow, deep slot canyon cut into conglomerate rock near the Sossusvlei dune field.

places.name: Skeleton Coast
places.why: Fog-bound dunes meet a cold, wreck-strewn Atlantic shoreline; the park requires prior permission for drones.

places.name: Fish River Canyon
places.why: Africa's largest canyon, a 160km gash carved by the Fish River through the southern Namibian plateau.

places.name: Okavango Delta
places.why: An inland river delta fans into thousands of channels and islets; concessions here require drone permits.

places.name: Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe side)
places.why: The Zambezi drops 108m in a sheet more than a kilometre wide; the national park restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Batoka Gorge
places.why: A zig-zagging basalt gorge carries the Zambezi downstream of the falls; the same park drone rules apply nearby.

places.name: Danakil Depression (Dallol)
places.why: Sulphur-yellow hydrothermal fields and salt flats sit below sea level in one of Earth's hottest places.

places.name: Erta Ale lava lake
places.why: One of the world's few persistent lava lakes glows inside a remote shield volcano's caldera.

places.name: Mount Kilimanjaro (Uhuru Peak)
places.why: Africa's highest summit still carries retreating glaciers; the national park requires a TANAPA drone permit.

places.name: Ngorongoro Crater
places.why: A vast, unbroken volcanic caldera holds its own resident wildlife population; drones require a conservation-area permit.

places.name: Nungwi Beach, Zanzibar
places.why: Turquoise shallows and dhow sails off the northern tip of Zanzibar island.

places.name: Erg Chebbi dunes
places.why: Saharan dunes over 150m tall, close enough to Merzouga village for a sunrise flight.

places.name: Erg Chigaga dunes
places.why: A more remote, less-visited dune sea than Erg Chebbi, reached by 4x4 from M'Hamid.

places.name: Chefchaouen
places.why: A hill town painted almost entirely blue, its rooftops reading as a single pattern from above.

places.name: Blyde River Canyon
places.why: One of the largest green canyons on Earth, with the Three Rondavels and Bourke's Luck Potholes.

places.name: Cape Point
places.why: Cliffs at the tip of the Cape Peninsula where two oceans are said to meet; the park requires a SANParks permit for drones.

places.name: Chott el Djerid
places.why: A vast, shimmering salt pan crossed by a single causeway road through the Tunisian Sahara.

places.name: Wadi Rum
places.why: Red sand and towering sandstone jebels used as a stand-in for Mars on screen; the protected area requires a drone permit.

places.name: Jebel Shams rim
places.why: Called Arabia's Grand Canyon, a sheer 1000m drop off Oman's highest mountain.

places.name: Wahiba (Sharqiya) Sands
places.why: Rippled orange dunes run to the horizon a short drive from Oman's coast.

places.name: Palm Jumeirah
places.why: An artificial palm-shaped island visible only as a pattern from the air; UAE drone flights need a GCAA permit.

places.name: The World Islands
places.why: Hundreds of small artificial islands arranged into a rough world map off the Dubai coast.

places.name: Liwa dunes
places.why: Some of the tallest dunes in Arabia, near the edge of the Empty Quarter.

places.name: Socotra Island
places.why: Dragon's blood trees and endemic flora on an island so isolated it looks alien from above.

places.name: Zhangye Danxia
places.why: Mineral-striped sandstone ridges in red, orange and gold, folded like a rainbow-coloured layer cake.

places.name: Zhangjiajie Grand Canyon
places.why: A glass-bottomed bridge spans a forested sandstone canyon near the pillars that inspired Avatar.

places.name: Yuanyang Rice Terraces
places.why: Terraces built by the Hani people over centuries flood and mirror the sky each winter.

places.name: Longji Rice Terraces
places.why: Dragon's-backbone terraces wrap steep hillsides in curved contour lines.

places.name: Li River karst (Guilin)
places.why: Limestone karst peaks stand in rows along the river; China requires drone registration and often a local flight permit.

places.name: Ha Long Bay
places.why: Thousands of limestone karst islands rise from emerald water; flights here require local authority approval.

places.name: Trang An Landscape Complex
places.why: Limestone karst towers and caves thread through rice paddies and slow rivers south of Hanoi.

places.name: Mu Cang Chai Rice Terraces
places.why: Contour terraces climb steep valley walls, turning gold at harvest.

places.name: Muong Hoa Valley (Sa Pa)
places.why: Terraced rice fields fill a valley below Vietnam's highest mountain, farmed by Hmong and Dao communities.

places.name: Banaue Rice Terraces
places.why: Two-thousand-year-old terraces climb the mountains of Ifugao, often called the eighth wonder of the world.

places.name: Batad Rice Terraces
places.why: An amphitheatre of terraces around the village of Batad, reachable only on foot.

places.name: El Nido lagoons
places.why: Limestone karst islets enclose hidden turquoise lagoons off Palawan's northern tip.

places.name: Mount Bromo
places.why: An active cinder cone smokes inside a vast volcanic sea of sand at sunrise.

places.name: Kelimutu crater lakes
places.why: Three crater lakes on one volcano shift colour independently, from turquoise to black to rust.

places.name: Ijen Crater
places.why: Sulphur mining and electric-blue "blue fire" flames light an acid crater lake before dawn.

places.name: Tegallalang Rice Terraces
places.why: Balinese subak-irrigated terraces step down a river valley just outside Ubud.

places.name: Kelingking Beach
places.why: A cliff shaped like a T-rex head frames a hidden white beach far below.

places.name: Wayag Islands, Raja Ampat
places.why: Karst islets scattered across a lagoon, the signature Raja Ampat view from a viewpoint climb.

places.name: Anak Krakatau
places.why: A young volcanic island rebuilding itself in the strait where its parent, Krakatoa, erupted catastrophically in 1883.

places.name: Railay Beach
places.why: Limestone karst towers wall off a beach reachable only by longtail boat.

places.name: Maya Bay, Phi Phi Leh
places.why: A cliff-ringed cove made famous by film; Thailand restricts drones in this marine park without a permit.

places.name: James Bond Island
places.why: A limestone karst tower stands alone in a bay of similar islets north of Phuket.

places.name: Mount Fuji
places.why: Japan's iconic, near-symmetrical volcanic cone; drones are commonly restricted near the summit trails and shrines.

places.name: Baltoro Glacier (Concordia)
places.why: Four of the world's fourteen 8000m peaks ring a glacier confluence reached only by multi-day trek; Pakistan requires a drone NOC.

places.name: Nubra Valley dunes
places.why: Cold-desert sand dunes sit at 3000m between snow peaks; this border region often denies Indian drone permits.

places.name: Great Rann of Kutch
places.why: A white salt desert stretches to the horizon, hosting a festival on full-moon nights; a border-zone drone permit is required.

places.name: Sam Sand Dunes
places.why: Thar Desert dunes near the Pakistan border, worked by camel safaris at sunset; drone flights here need an Indian permit.

places.name: Everest region (Khumbu)
places.why: The world's highest icefall and glaciers surround Everest Base Camp; Nepal restricts drone flights near the mountain.

places.name: Twelve Apostles
places.why: Limestone sea stacks stand offshore along a coastline that is still actively collapsing.

places.name: Loch Ard Gorge
places.why: A collapsed sea cave and gorge near the Twelve Apostles, with a dramatic wave-cut arch.

places.name: Whitehaven Beach
places.why: Pure silica sand swirls with turquoise water at Hill Inlet; part of a marine park with zoned flight restrictions.

places.name: Heart Reef
places.why: A naturally heart-shaped coral formation, viewable only from the air inside a no-fly buffer over the reef.

places.name: Uluru
places.why: The sandstone monolith at Australia's centre; Parks Australia bans all drone flights over Uluru itself.

places.name: Kata Tjuta
places.why: Domed rock formations beside Uluru, under the same park-wide drone ban.

places.name: Kings Canyon
places.why: Sheer sandstone walls drop 100m to a valley floor of ancient palms and cycads.

places.name: Bungle Bungle Range
places.why: Orange-and-black striped beehive domes rise from the Kimberley; the park requires a drone permit.

places.name: Pinnacles Desert
places.why: Thousands of limestone spires stand in yellow sand north of Perth.

places.name: Lake Hillier
places.why: A permanently bubblegum-pink lake sits inside a nature reserve with restricted access.

places.name: Shell Beach, Shark Bay
places.why: A beach made entirely of tiny white cockle shells, sometimes 10m deep, in a World Heritage bay.

places.name: Milford Sound
places.why: Sheer glacier-carved walls drop straight into a fjord; the park requires a Department of Conservation concession for drones.

places.name: Franz Josef Glacier
places.why: A temperate glacier descends almost to sea level through rainforest; DOC restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
places.why: Volcanic craters and the vivid Emerald Lakes along a one-day crossing on a mountain sacred to Māori.

places.name: Wai-O-Tapu
places.why: Geothermal terraces and craters in acid greens and oranges bubble across a volcanic field.

places.name: Pancake Rocks
places.why: Layered limestone stacks that look like piled pancakes, with blowholes at high tide.

places.name: Bora Bora lagoon
places.why: An almost impossibly turquoise lagoon rings a volcanic island under a barrier reef.

places.name: Yasawa Islands
places.why: A chain of volcanic islands strung along clear water northwest of Fiji's main island.

places.name: Mount Yasur
places.why: One of the world's most accessible active volcanoes, throwing lava bombs visible after dark; local permits are required.

places.name: Rabaul Caldera
places.why: A drowned volcanic caldera with active cones still steaming beside the harbour town it half-destroyed in 1994.

places.name: Nā Pali Coast
places.why: Fluted green cliffs drop straight into the Pacific with no road access; Hawaii state parks commonly restrict drone launches.

places.name: Waimea Canyon
places.why: Called the "Grand Canyon of the Pacific"; a Hawaii state park where drone launches are commonly restricted.

places.name: Bixby Bridge, Big Sur
places.why: A concrete arch bridge over a coastal canyon on Highway 1, one of the most-photographed spans in the US.

places.name: Antelope Canyon
places.why: Light beams pierce a sculpted sandstone slot canyon; the Navajo Nation bans drones here without a hard-to-get tribal permit.

places.name: Horseshoe Bend
places.region: Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, Arizona
places.why: The Colorado River bends 270 degrees around a sandstone butte; this NPS unit bans drones without a permit.

places.name: Monument Valley
places.why: Sandstone buttes rise from the desert floor in the classic Western-movie skyline; the Navajo Nation restricts drone use.

places.name: Havasu Falls
places.why: Turquoise, travertine-lined falls deep in a side canyon of the Grand Canyon; the Havasupai Tribe does not permit visitor drones.

places.name: Grand Canyon (Mather Point)
places.why: A mile-deep gorge cut by the Colorado River; the National Park Service bans drones inside all national parks.

places.name: Bonneville Salt Flats
places.why: A dead-flat salt pan used for land-speed records, mirror-like after rain.

places.name: Antelope Island
places.why: An island of bison and salt-crusted shoreline in the middle of a shrinking inland sea.

places.name: Delicate Arch
places.why: A freestanding sandstone arch on a slickrock bowl; a national park where the NPS bans drones.

places.name: The Wave
places.why: Undulating striped sandstone reached only by a lottery-issued BLM permit.

places.name: Bisti/De-Na-Zin Wilderness
places.why: Eroded hoodoos and badlands in a federally designated Wilderness, where rules commonly bar motorized equipment like drones.

places.name: White Sands
places.region: White Sands National Park, New Mexico
places.why: Gypsum dunes so white they look like snow; the National Park Service bans drones here as in all national parks.

places.name: Great Sand Dunes
places.why: The tallest dunes in North America, backed by a 14,000ft mountain range; the NPS bans drones in this national park.

places.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
places.why: Rippled dunes in the hottest, driest US national park, where the NPS bans all drone flights.

places.name: Racetrack Playa
places.why: Rocks leave long trails across a cracked dry lakebed; also inside a national park where drones are banned.

places.name: Zion Narrows
places.why: The Virgin River carves a slot canyon barely wider than the water itself; the NPS bans drones in this national park.

places.name: Bryce Canyon Amphitheater
places.why: Thousands of red hoodoo spires fill a natural amphitheatre; another national park where the NPS bans drones.

places.name: Yosemite Falls
places.why: North America's tallest waterfall drops in three tiers off a granite cliff; the NPS bans drones throughout the park.

places.name: Crater Lake
places.why: The deepest lake in the US fills a collapsed volcano's caldera; the NPS bans drones in this national park.

places.name: Multnomah Falls
places.why: A two-tiered waterfall with a footbridge partway up; the Gorge is a National Scenic Area with its own drone restrictions.

places.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
places.why: The largest hot spring in the US, its colour bands are best read from directly above; the NPS bans drones here.

places.name: Paradise, Mount Rainier
places.why: Wildflower meadows below a glaciated volcano; the NPS bans drones throughout this national park.

places.name: Steptoe Butte (Palouse)
places.why: Rolling wheat-farm hills form curved patterns of light and shadow, especially at harvest.

places.name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes
places.why: Wind-blown coral-coloured dunes eroded from nearby sandstone cliffs, at a state park in southern Utah.

places.name: Matanuska Glacier
places.why: One of the few Alaskan glaciers reachable by road, riddled with blue crevasses and ice caves.

places.name: Mendenhall Glacier
places.why: A glacier and ice caves near Juneau, inside a national forest where the Forest Service restricts drones near the visitor centre.

places.name: Niagara Falls (Table Rock)
places.why: The Horseshoe Falls plunge in a curtain of mist; nearby airspace and Ontario Parks rules restrict drone flights.

places.name: Moraine Lake
places.why: Glacial silt turns this lake an impossible turquoise below the Valley of the Ten Peaks; Parks Canada requires a drone permit.

places.name: Peyto Lake
places.why: A wolf-head-shaped, glacier-fed lake seen from the Icefields Parkway; the same Parks Canada drone rules apply.

places.name: Athabasca Glacier
places.why: A tongue of the Columbia Icefield reaches down to the Icefields Parkway; Parks Canada requires a permit for drones.

places.name: Copper Canyon (Divisadero)
places.why: A system of canyons larger and deeper than the Grand Canyon, crossed by a spectacular rail line.

places.name: Arenal Volcano
places.why: A near-perfect volcanic cone above a lake and rainforest; the national park restricts drones without a SINAC permit.

places.name: Poás Volcano
places.why: One of the world's largest active craters, often filled with a turquoise acid lake; the same national-park drone rules apply.

places.name: Pacaya Volcano
places.why: An active volcano with fresh lava fields you can hike across from the crater rim.

places.name: Iguazú Falls (Devil's Throat)
places.why: Nearly 300 cascades spread across two countries; the national parks on both sides commonly restrict drones.

places.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
places.region: Los Glaciares National Park, Santa Cruz
places.why: One of the few advancing glaciers on Earth, regularly calving huge slabs into the lake; the park restricts drones.

places.name: Salinas Grandes
places.why: A blinding white salt flat high in the Andes, criss-crossed by hand-dug drainage lines.

places.name: Ischigualasto (Valle de la Luna)
places.why: Wind-eroded rock formations in a lunar-looking desert valley, a UNESCO fossil site requiring flight authorization.

places.name: Torres del Paine
places.why: Granite towers rise straight out of the Patagonian steppe above glacial lakes; the national park requires a CONAF drone permit.

places.name: Marble Caves
places.why: Wave-carved marble caverns line the shore of a glacial lake, their colours shifting with the water level.

places.name: Valle de la Luna, Atacama
places.why: Salt-crusted dunes and eroded ridges in the driest desert on Earth; the reserve restricts drones without a CONAF permit.

places.name: Villarrica Volcano
places.why: A snow-capped, persistently active volcano with a glowing lava lake; the national park requires drone authorization.

places.name: Salar de Uyuni
places.why: The world's largest salt flat turns into a mirror after rain, erasing the horizon.

places.name: Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca)
places.why: Mineral bands paint a high-altitude ridge in stripes of red, gold and lavender.

places.name: Colca Canyon
places.why: One of the world's deepest canyons, where Andean condors ride the morning thermals over the Cruz del Cóndor.

places.name: Machu Picchu
places.why: Inca agricultural terraces wrap a mountaintop citadel; Peru's Ministry of Culture bans drone flights over the site.

places.name: Cotopaxi Volcano
places.why: One of the world's highest active volcanoes, a near-perfect snow-capped cone; the national park restricts drones.

places.name: Angel Falls
places.why: The world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall drops off a tepui inside a remote national park with restricted airspace.

places.name: Kaieteur Falls
places.why: One of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls on Earth, deep in untouched rainforest; flights need government authorization.

places.name: Chapada Diamantina
places.why: Table-top mountains, canyons and waterfalls in Brazil's interior highlands; the national park restricts drones without a permit.

places.name: Fernando de Noronha
places.why: A volcanic archipelago with some of Brazil's clearest water; a marine national park that restricts drone flights.

places.name: Lençóis Maranhenses
places.why: White sand dunes fill with rainwater lagoons each year, forming thousands of turquoise pools; the park restricts drones.

places.name: Ilulissat Icefjord
places.why: Icebergs calved from one of the world's fastest glaciers drift down a fjord toward the open sea.

places.name: Lemaire Channel
places.why: A narrow, iceberg-choked strait between cliffs; no single authority governs the airspace, and IAATO guidelines discourage drones near wildlife.

places.name: Cabo de Gata volcanic coast
places.why: Volcanic cliffs and hidden coves in Spain's driest region, inside a protected natural park.

places.name: Vestmannaeyjar (Heimaey)
places.why: A volcanic archipelago where a 1973 eruption swallowed half the town; puffin cliffs and a fresh lava field surround it.

places.name: Askja Caldera
places.why: A remote volcanic caldera holding a milky geothermal crater lake, reached by rough highland tracks.

places.name: Fagradalsfjall lava field
places.why: Fresh black lava from a series of 2021-2024 eruptions spreads across a peninsula near Reykjavík.

places.name: Vatnajökull ice caves
places.why: Blue glacier ice caves form each winter under Europe's largest ice cap, inside a national park with drone limits.

places.name: Ras al-Jinz turtle coast
places.why: A remote turtle-nesting beach where dunes meet the Arabian Sea at the edge of Oman's Empty Quarter.

places.name: Empty Quarter dunes (Rub' al Khali)
places.why: The world's largest contiguous sand desert, with dunes over 250m tall; Saudi Arabia requires a drone import and flight permit.

places.name: AlUla (Elephant Rock)
places.why: Wind-sculpted sandstone monoliths rise from a desert valley beside ancient Nabatean tombs.

places.name: Deadvlei clay pan
places.why: Blackened camel-thorn skeletons stand in a white clay pan surrounded by the tallest dunes on Earth.

places.name: Richtersveld
places.why: A mountainous desert of succulents and eroded rock along the lower Orange River.

places.name: Comoé/Sahel dunes (Termit)
places.why: Isolated sandstone massifs rise from Saharan dune fields in one of the least-visited desert landscapes on Earth.

places.name: Serengeti kopjes
places.why: Granite outcrops break up an endless grass plain crossed each year by the wildebeest migration.

places.name: Sahara dunes, Ubari
places.why: Salt lakes sit between towering dunes deep in the Libyan Sahara, among the most remote in the world.

places.name: Pinnacle Point coastal caves
places.why: Sea cliffs and caves along the Garden Route coast, an early-human archaeological site above the surf.

places.name: Aogashima Caldera
places.why: A village sits inside a volcano within a volcano, on a remote island reachable mostly by helicopter or ferry.

places.name: Jeju Island lava tubes & coast
places.why: Volcanic cones (oreum) and black lava-rock coastline ring a shield volcano island; Jeju restricts drones near the crater and airport.

places.name: Guilin Yangshuo karst
places.why: Conical karst peaks along the Li and Yulong rivers, among the most-painted landscapes in Chinese art.

places.name: Detian Falls
places.why: A wide, tiered transboundary waterfall on the China-Vietnam border, in a sensitive border zone requiring flight approval.

places.name: Bali Sea rice terraces (Jatiluwih)
places.why: A UNESCO subak-irrigated terrace system spreading down the slopes of a volcano.

places.name: Palawan's Coron lagoons
places.why: Limestone cliffs enclose hidden turquoise lakes and lagoons around sunken WWII wrecks.

places.name: Boracay's White Beach
places.why: A four-kilometre arc of fine white sand on a small island, seen best from directly overhead at low tide.

places.name: Bai Tu Long Bay
places.why: A quieter neighbour to Ha Long Bay with the same limestone karst islands and far fewer boats.

places.name: Similan Islands
places.why: Granite boulder islands ring clear water inside a marine national park with seasonal closures and drone limits.

places.name: Ko Kradan reef flats
places.why: Shallow reef flats and a sandbar shift shape with the tide off a small Andaman island.

places.name: Uyuni train cemetery & salt hotel margin
places.why: Rusting steam locomotives sit abandoned at the edge of the salt flat, a smaller companion shot to the salar itself.

places.name: Pantanal wetlands
places.why: The world's largest tropical wetland floods into a maze of channels and lagoons each rainy season.

places.name: Uspallata/Aconcagua foothills
places.why: Red and ochre eroded badlands below the highest peak in the Americas.

places.name: Tepuis of Canaima (Roraima)
places.why: Flat-topped table mountains rise sheer from the jungle, inside a national park with restricted drone airspace.

places.name: Great Blue Hole
places.why: A near-perfect circle of deep blue water inside a barrier reef, formed by a collapsed limestone cave.

places.name: Bay Islands reef (Roatán)
places.why: Coral reef patterns and cayes visible through clear Caribbean water off Honduras's largest bay island.

places.name: Cenotes of Yucatán (Ik Kil)
places.why: A circular sinkhole cenote drops through jungle to a pool far below, one of thousands riddling the peninsula.

places.name: Morning Glory Pool
places.why: A cluster of vividly coloured hot springs and geysers along the Firehole River; NPS bans drones park-wide.

places.name: Denali & the Alaska Range
places.why: North America's tallest peak and its glaciers dominate a vast wilderness where the NPS bans drone flights.

places.name: Glacier National Park (Grinnell Glacier)
places.why: Retreating glaciers and turquoise tarns along the Continental Divide, in a national park that bans drones.

places.name: Badlands National Park
places.why: Layered, wind-carved buttes and spires stretch across the prairie; the NPS bans drones in this national park.

places.name: Hells Canyon
places.why: North America's deepest river gorge, cut by the Snake River between Idaho and Oregon.

places.name: Columbia Icefield
places.why: A vast icefield feeding several major glaciers, crossed by a glacier-adapted vehicle tour; Parks Canada requires a drone permit.

places.name: Baffin Island fjords
places.why: Arctic fjords and towering granite walls along one of the least-visited coastlines on Earth.
